history.summary: CSV TOWN ERROR CORRECTED: this temple is NOT in Shimoga - it stands at Sharavu Mahaganapathy Temple Road, opposite Ideal Towers, Hampankatta, in the heart of Mangaluru city, Dakshina Kannada district (exact location 12.870423, 74.840864 per the temple's official site). 'Sharavu' comes from 'shara' (arrow): legend says Tuluva king Maharaja Veerabahu (called Bharadwaj in one account) accidentally killed a cow with an arrow meant for a tiger; on sage Bharadhwaja's advice he installed a Shiva linga at the spot as penance, worshipped as Sharabeshwara, and built the tank Sharatheertha. The temple later became famous as Mahaganapathi's shrine after the divine image of Dashabhuja (ten-armed) Mahaganapathi is said to have appeared on the temple's southern wall. Two presiding deities: Lord Shiva (seen first on entry) and Lord Ganesha on the south side. Roughly 800 years old and a major Tulunadu religious-cultural centre, hosting Yakshagana, dance, drama and social-service activities. The complex also houses shrines associated with Kadri, Mangaladevi and Kudroli deities. Timings conflict across sources (official site sharavu.org lists 6:00 AM-8:30 PM daily; travel sites list 5:00 AM-12:00 PM and 4:30-8:00 PM); verify locally.

name: Shri Sharavu Mahaganapathi Temple
town_description: Mangaluru (Mangalore) is a major port city on Karnataka's southwest coast and the commercial and cultural hub of Tulunadu. The Sharavu temple sits in Hampankatta, the city centre, about 1 km from Mangaluru Central railway station.
